name: hide_invert_vertex_mark
description: Frozen reference behaviour: after a hide-invert issued with the selection type set to VERTICES, a vertex whose only polygon has just become hidden still reads NOT hidden — and stays that way until a hide operation touches that specific vertex. The vertex hide plane is therefore derived INCREMENTALLY, over the elements an operation touches; it is neither a stored bit that is never derived, nor a derivation that re-runs globally whenever hiding is applied. Both of those simpler readings are refuted here, each by a named row.
source: Frozen reference capture (headless, scripted): one process per case so no attribute or selection state can leak between them; seven trigger cases plus one that did not discriminate.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (case script + per-case result JSON live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: Every case re-runs the whole prefix from an empty scene and asserts the anomaly reproduced before applying its trigger; it reproduced in all seven. The rig's premise — that the probed vertex has valence ONE — is asserted BY the case, because a vertex sharing a still-visible polygon is hidden under neither reading and would make the entire experiment vacuous.

parameters.notes: drive record read from the private capture harness, hide_semantics/vertmark_case.py:162-183; The private case script is the drive record and EVERY command in it is bare — no arguments anywhere — so all values maps are empty except the one thing that is a real mode argument: the SELECTION TYPE the hide and the invert are issued under. That is not inferred from prose; the fixture carries it in two machine-readable keys (prefix.selection_type_before_hide / _before_invert, lines 48-49) and says in its own words that they exist so a driver can execute and read them back. The common prefix (hide, then the vertex-mode invert) is the operation under test and is repeated on every cell; the rig build and the polygon selections are stand. Two cells drive nothing beyond that prefix and carry only it: `none` is the control (a bare re-read) and `selection_type_roundtrip`'s trigger is a selection-type switch, i.e. stand. Op names are vibe3d's public ids (source/commands/mesh/hide.d:368,535,623). ONE mapping to flag: the capture fired two DIFFERENT unhide commands — a bare selection-scoped one for `unhide_with_spare_selected` (vertmark_case.py:242) and an unhide-ALL for `clear_then_rehide` (vertmark_case.py:288) — recorded here as the same logical op separated by an `all` flag, following parameters_extract._parse_argstring's own convention that a lone positional becomes {token: true}. vibe3d has a public counterpart for the all-arm only (`mesh.unhideAll`); the selection-scoped arm has none, which is why the neutral logical name is used for both. An 8th cell is included beyond `rows`: the fixture's `non_discriminating` block is a real recorded case (it just carries no information about the law) and dropping it would hide a driven cell.

rig.comment: A 3x3 quad grid PLUS a disconnected spare quad parked far away on +X, sharing no vertices with the grid. The spare exists so there is a genuinely unrelated polygon available as a trigger.
rig.probe_vertex_valence_is_load_bearing: A vertex with more than one incident polygon would still have a visible polygon and would be un-hidden under BOTH readings, so no trigger could separate them. Assert this or the fixture asserts nothing.

prefix.comment: The common state every trigger case reaches. Hiding the spare as well as the grid corner is what leaves the spare VISIBLE after the invert — which is what makes an unrelated, still-hideable polygon available.
steps: with the selection type set to polygons, select grid polygon 0 and the spare polygon 9, then hide the selection
switch the selection type to vertices
prefix.why_the_types_are_machine_readable: `steps` above is prose. These two fields are the SAME claim in a form a driver can EXECUTE and then READ BACK, and a driver must take its type from them rather than from the prose. The first driver of this fixture performed steps 1 and 3 and silently skipped step 2, and stayed green — because on the pre-0628 engine the invert ignores the selection type, so BOTH modes yield the identical polygon set and the identical probe value. No numeric assertion could have separated them; only reading the type back can.

after_invert.the_anomaly: grid polygon 0 IS hidden and it is the probe vertex's only polygon, yet the probe vertex reads 0

rows.trigger: no operation at all; read the probe vertex twice more
rows.role: control — the value is STABLE under a bare re-read. Without this, any later flip could be a read-ordering artefact rather than a re-derivation.
a REAL hide was applied and the probe vertex stayed stale, so the derivation is not global

rows.trigger: hide grid polygon 4, which is already hidden — the hidden set does not change at all
rows.role: second, independent refutation of the global reading

rows.trigger: switch the selection type to polygons and back to vertices; no visibility operation at all
rows.role: separates 'any command re-derives' from 'the hide path re-derives' — the weakest possible trigger, and it does nothing

rows.trigger: hide grid polygon 0 — the probe vertex's OWN polygon — which is already hidden, so no polygon bit changes
rows.role: THE row. No polygon bit changes and the vertex flips anyway, so something recomputed it — and it recomputed only because the operation named the probe vertex's own polygon.

rows.trigger: with the selection type set to vertices and the probe vertex selected, hide the selection
rows.role: second, independent refutation, driven from the vertex side rather than the polygon side

rows.trigger: unhide everything, then re-hide grid polygon 0 the ordinary way
rows.role: the plane RESUMES deriving normally once the state is cleared, so the invert's own write is a latch on a normally-derived plane rather than the plane never being derived

non_discriminating.trigger: unhide with only the spare selected
non_discriminating.status: DID NOT DISCRIMINATE — recorded as such, not as evidence
non_discriminating.why: The unhide cleared the hidden set ENTIRELY, so the probe vertex's polygon was no longer hidden. After that both readings predict 0; the row carries no information about which is right.
non_discriminating.worth_knowing_anyway: A selection-scoped unhide un-hid everything, not just the selection.

conclusion.law: The vertex hide plane is derived INCREMENTALLY, over the elements the operation touches. A hide-invert writes the vertex plane directly and leaves exactly the entries whose derived value it contradicts stale.

classification.detail: Since 0628 landed (2026-08-09) vibe3d's hide-invert is COMPONENT-TYPED: in vertex mode it flips the vertex plane the selection type names and propagates upward, so the post-invert polygon set matches the reference's nine grid polygons. What remains — permanently, by decision — is that our vertex plane is re-derived TOTALLY from the polygon plane after every mutation, so we have no stale window at all: the probe vertex reads 1 under its now-hidden polygon where the reference reads 0 off a stale entry. The two divergences below moved in opposite directions exactly as the fixture predicted they would.

vibe3d_measured.comment: The AGREEMENT rows only. The post-invert row is not here: it is where the two engines part, so it lives in `divergences` below — one frozen number, one owner, one status, rather than a second copy that can drift.

classification.unrepresentable_here: The 'hide an already-hidden polygon' trigger cannot be expressed in vibe3d: a hidden face cannot be selected (hidden and selected are mutually exclusive), and a hide with an empty selection hides EVERYTHING — so attempting that row hides all ten polygons rather than being the no-op the reference makes it.

divergences.comment: TWO divergences live in this one prefix and they have OPPOSITE futures, so they carry separate statuses. One is a gap that is being closed; the other is a deliberate design decision that must never be closed. A single expected/not-expected flag covering both would, on the day the first closes, either retire the second along with it or refuse to retire either.

invert_face_set.what: While this was open, the reference hid the nine grid polygons after the prefix and vibe3d hid eight: our invert was a plain polygon flip that ignored the selection type, so it flipped the two originally-hidden polygons back to VISIBLE instead of flipping the vertex plane the type names and propagating upward. CLOSED by 0628 — the invert now flips the plane the selection type names, and the face set matches.
invert_face_set.closes_when: 0628 makes the invert component-typed. vibe3d's post-invert hidden set then becomes the reference's, and the marker assertion in the test goes red. A red THERE means the gap CLOSED, not that something broke.
invert_face_set.closed_how: 0628 landed as `hide: the invert flips the plane the selection names, with no model change needed`. The marker fired exactly as built. Notably it did NOT require the model change the task predicted: because the vertex plane is a pure function of the face plane, `flip the vertices and propagate up` is a closed transformation OF the face plane, so the typed invert is expressible with our derivation left TOTAL — which is why the face set converged while `vertex_plane_derivation` below did not.
invert_face_set.retire_by: setting `status` to "closed" — AND re-freezing `vertex_plane_derivation.vibe3d_probe_after_invert` to the value the closed face set implies. Those are one change, not two independent ones: the probe read 0 only WHILE this gap was open and polygon 0 was left visible. The test cross-checks the two frozen rows against vibe3d's own derivation law, so editing one without the other fails loudly instead of freezing a contradiction. Done on 2026-08-09: the probe moved 0 → 1 in the same edit.

vertex_plane_derivation.what: vibe3d derives the vertex hide plane TOTALLY after every mutation; the reference derives it INCREMENTALLY over the elements an operation touches, so its invert leaves exactly the contradicted entries stale. Same probe, different law.
vertex_plane_derivation.kind: deliberate design decision, not a gap
vertex_plane_derivation.the_two_numbers_agreed_by_accident_until: They used to both read 0, for unrelated reasons: the reference's 0 was a STALE entry sitting under a HIDDEN polygon 0, vibe3d's 0 was a correct derivation under a VISIBLE polygon 0. The fixture predicted that closing `invert_face_set` would make polygon 0 hidden here too and push the totally-derived probe to 1 while the reference stayed 0. That is exactly what happened on 2026-08-09. The former agreement was never evidence that the laws agreed, and this disagreement is not evidence that anything broke — it is the same law, finally visible as a different number.
vertex_plane_derivation.never_close: This entry has no open/closed toggle and must not acquire one. Reproducing the stale read means threading a touched-set through the derivation that rides EVERY geometry-mutating commit, in order to ship a value a user would file as a bug; undo already serves the round trip. A future reader must not 'fix' vibe3d's total derivation to chase the reference's 0.

consequence_involution.what: Our vertex-mode invert is NOT its own inverse. Press it twice from the prefix state and the hidden set does not come back: [0,9] → [0..8] → [9]. Re-deriving the vertex plane after the first press destroys the distinction the flipped plane carried, so the second press has different input than the round trip needs. In POLYGON mode the invert is still an involution: [0,9] → [1..8] → [0,9].
consequence_involution.why_it_is_here: It is not an independent finding — it is the SAME total-vs-incremental decision above, observed one press later. The reference's staleness is precisely what would make its round trip work.
consequence_involution.why_it_is_NOT_a_third_divergence: A divergence row in this fixture carries a frozen `reference_*` number, and there is no capture behind a reference double-invert: the 0628 Ph0 capture ran seven triggers after ONE invert and never pressed it twice. Writing a reference value here would mean INFERRING a measurement from the frozen law and filing it as observed. Recorded instead as a one-sided, vibe3d-only consequence — absent on the reference side, not negative. Same discipline as `not_covered` in the sibling subdivide fixture.
consequence_involution.measured_how: vibe3d-only, driven over the same HTTP prefix this fixture already drives — no reference engine involved, so these two rows are live-checkable rather than frozen prose.
consequence_involution.guards_what: The polygon-mode row is the contrast that makes the vertex-mode row mean something: without it, 'not an involution' would be indistinguishable from 'the invert is simply broken'. Together they also give `never_close` teeth — an implementation that acquired the reference's stale window to chase its 0 would very likely make the vertex-mode double press an involution again, and this row would go red.
consequence_involution.undo_is_unaffected: Undo remains the exact round trip; the second press is not how a user returns.
